article: Affiliate marketing measurement: tracking, conversion, ITP, and server-to-server postbacks
scope: Corrected the Japanese source and completed full AI reviews of all twelve available language editions. Exact source and translation hashes are recorded for each review. Publication is pending.
findings: Removed claims that every affiliate link must redirect through an ASP and that tracking IDs are always available from ASP cookies.
Reframed WebKit ITP behavior with its applicable Safari conditions; it is not a universal 24-hour/7-day expiry rule for all cookies.
Clarified that server-to-server measurement can improve data control but does not bypass browser restrictions or consent requirements and still needs failure/retry/duplicate handling.
Corrected claims that fingerprinting is a reliable unique identifier, S2S prevents fraud or guarantees complete measurement, and clean rooms automatically guarantee privacy.
Added primary technical references for WebKit tracking prevention, Google server-side tagging, and IETF redirect semantics.

post/affiliate-marketing-mechanism/index.summary: Read the complete English edition against the Japanese source. Corrected universal claims about ASP redirects, third-party cookies, fixed ITP expiry windows, S2S bypass/reliability, fingerprinting, and privacy guarantees; added primary technical references.

meaning.note: Compared all sections with the Japanese source and aligned the tracking flow, Safari/WebKit limitations, S2S scope, privacy caveats, and conclusion.

terminology.note: Checked affiliate/ASP, Click ID, first- and third-party cookies, LocalStorage, ITP, S2S/postback, conversion events, fingerprinting, and data clean room terminology.

mathematics.note: No formulas or calculations occur. The 24-hour and seven-day storage behaviors are bounded to cited WebKit conditions and explicitly not presented as universal rules.

code.note: Reviewed both Mermaid flows, example URLs, HTTP 302/307/301 semantics, and technical identifiers; there are no executable code samples.

links.note: Checked internal English links against published article slugs and added five primary technical references to WebKit, Google for Developers, and IETF RFC 9110.

limitations: Review performed by Codex (AI); no human editor or native English-language reviewer has confirmed style or terminology.
Browser tracking-prevention behavior can change; the article bounds examples to WebKit documentation and recommends checking current behavior.
This general technical overview is not legal advice or a guarantee that a specific attribution implementation complies with any jurisdiction's requirements.
